search_log: Searched “Virginia Woolf The Years novel excerpt publisher”; Google Books and publisher records yielded only snippets or catalog copy, not a usable publisher-hosted extract.

Searched “Virginia Woolf The Years narrative point of view third person scholarly” and variants involving narrator and free indirect discourse; opened the PALA scholarly PDF and Open Library description.

Searched for the full text through Internet Archive and Open Library; the library edition was preview-only, while the Virginia Woolf Project supplied a readable complete text that was sampled in the opening, middle, and final section.

Ran targeted site:.edu and site:.ac.uk searches for The Years with “third person” and “narrator”; UCL and Westminster dissertation PDFs timed out or provided only search snippets, so they were not used as evidence.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third-person, moving among the Pargiter characters through external narration, psychonarration, and free-indirect discourse. Numerous first-person forms in the quotes are explicitly tagged character thoughts, remembered speech, or direct dialogue, and the apparent narratorial “we” in q00018 is itself a character’s imagined novelist voice. Quote evidence agrees independently with scholarly whole-book analysis, the Open Library structural description, and prose sampled across the complete online text. No sustained first- or second-person base section was found; the only residual limitation is that the complete web transcription is not publisher-hosted.
